_readme: VERIFIED CORRECTIONS to the DERIVED platform board - applied by build-platform-board.js section 4.
WRITTEN BACK 2026-08-08/09, AND THAT IS WHAT THIS FILE IS NOW FOR: SHRINKING.
This file previously carried a WRITE-BACK QUEUE of 70 entries - 64 amendments plus 6 findings that
existed on the board and in NEITHER release document. All 70 have been written into
RELEASE-2.6.2-TRACKER.md and RELEASE-2.6.2-DEFECT-REGISTER.md, which are the documents the release
is certified against, and deleted from here. The correction layer is not the record.
The six board-only findings SWEEP-01..SWEEP-06 became register defects R262-D-98..R262-D-103. Each
heading names the sweep id it was logged under, so the board history is traceable in both
directions. They were renumbered because the register owns the defect id namespace, and a second
parallel namespace is the exact 'second board' this project keeps having to dismantle.
THE QUEUE IS NOW EMPTY. 2026-08-09: the last three entries are gone, and the reason is that the
thing blocking them got built rather than worked around.
This file used to say: 'WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY IT IS NOT LAZINESS. Three SEVERITY corrections, and
nothing else. Their substance - status, evidence, measurement - is in the tracker. The severity is
not, because RELEASE-2.6.2-TRACKER.md HAS NO SEVERITY COLUMN: the board infers P1 from the literal
string P0 appearing anywhere in a row, and P2 otherwise. Expressing these three in the document
would mean writing P0 into a row where it is false, or deleting a true sentence that happens to
contain it. Both are gaming the parser rather than recording a fact, so neither was done. THE
DURABLE FIX IS A SEVERITY COLUMN IN THE TRACKER, not three more rows here.'
That diagnosis was right and has been acted on. build-platform-board.js now reads an explicit
[SEV:Pn] marker from any tracker cell, and EXPLICIT BEATS INFERRED - the same rule the defect
register merge already enforced. A marker was chosen over a real column because a column means
realigning every row of every table in a 900-line document, and a miscounted row silently shifts
which cell is read as status. [SEV:Pn] rather than the register's middot form because in a table
cell that shape is ordinary prose punctuation and would eventually match a sentence that merely
MENTIONS a severity; [SEV:P1] cannot occur by accident in English.
R262-I-04, R262-I-08 and R262-WEB-01 now carry their severity IN THE TRACKER, each with the reason
for the re-assessment written beside it. Verified by deletion, not by assertion: with these three
entries removed from this file the board still reports P1/P1/P2 and sevExplicit true for all three.
Note the asymmetry that makes the marker honest - it is authoritative in BOTH directions and can
downgrade as well as upgrade, whereas the old /P0/ inference could only ever raise.
ONE FURTHER LIMIT, FOUND DURING THE WRITE-BACK AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ADDING ANYTHING HERE:
build-platform-board.js section 1 parses defect headings with the hard-coded pattern R262-D-<n>.
A register entry logged under any other id shape is invisible to the board no matter how well it
is written. That is why the sweep ids were renumbered rather than written in as-is.
DO NOT ADD A STATUS HERE THAT HAS NOT BEEN MEASURED. The sweep's own rule, unchanged.
DO NOT USE THIS FILE TO AVOID EDITING THE RELEASE RECORD. That is what it has just stopped being.

remove.why: PHANTOM. Not an issue — the markdown table header `| File | Shard | Guards | Status |` at RELEASE-2.6.2-TRACKER.md:614, parsed into an item with id `File`, title `Shard` and status OPEN. The generator now rejects table header rows structurally (a row whose next line is the `|---|` separator) and by id shape (a real id is hyphenated and carries a digit), so this cannot recur. Kept listed here so the deletion is a recorded decision rather than a row that quietly vanished.
